body.statement: Among all total simultaneous confidence systems with uniform coverage at least \(1-\gamma_0\) over \(\mathcal H_{\beta,D}(m)\), determine the minimax order of maximal log-width, prove a matching confidence-length lower bound, and characterize exactly the joint sequences for which an honest \(W_{n,m,\tau}\to0\) in probability exists. The derivation must decide whether the optimal width has the same sparse-versus-collective transition or selection factor as \(\mathcal R(n,m,\tau)\), rather than imposing that equality. For the converse, use the explicit family \((P^{\mathrm{lb}}_{\omega}:\omega\in\Omega_m)\) in the paired-cell Assouad--Fano confidence-width handle: prove that every member lies in the same fixed-\(m\) Hall class, bound the divergence between neighboring observed product experiments by an absolute constant, compute the separation between the corresponding \(m^{-1}\)-weighted policy-mixture log quantiles, and apply Assouad's lemma or Fano's inequality plus confidence-set testing duality to lower-bound maximal width.
body.justification: The explicit paired-splice hypercube makes the honest-width converse a concrete testing problem over policy mixtures, separate from expected regret.
body.gap: SasakiWang2024 establishes a scalar worst-case bias floor, while ChernozhukovLeeRosenSun2025 uses Gaussian maxima for regular policy values; the growing heterogeneous tail-mixture width frontier is not covered by either argument.
body.consumer: The result tells the OsamaZachariahStoica2020 workflow when an extreme-loss certificate can become informative uniformly over every feasible policy.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove a matching confidence-length lower bound over all total simultaneous systems and derive the necessary-and-sufficient joint-sequence condition for a shrinking maximal width, separately from policy regret.
obligation.obstruction: The paired family supplies bounded neighboring divergence, but confidence-set testing duality must retain the \(m^{-1}\)-weighted mixture separation for a growing collection of policies. A one-coordinate two-point argument is diluted by \(1/m\), whereas an Assouad mean-separation argument does not by itself lower-bound the maximum simultaneous interval length. No frozen result bridges that distinction. In addition, the current upper-system definition requires the emitted empty-region correction before its stochastic width claim is true.
obligation.attempted: I verified exact Bonferroni coverage from the \(4m\) binomial inversions, propagated Hall strips to core roots, and analyzed the paired-splice neighboring divergence. I also checked the empty-region fallback at boundary indices and found that its positive-probability global width invalidates the present shrinking-in-probability claim, motivating the definition correction in this bundle.
obligation.partial_result:
Exact binomial inversion and a union bound give simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\gamma_0\) for the corrected system because, on the joint count event, every true \((\alpha_{xa},\log c_{xa})\) belongs to its raw Hall region.  Multiplicative binomial inversion at \(T^{\mathrm{ci}}_{n,m}\) and \(eT^{\mathrm{ci}}_{n,m}\) gives the conservative stochastic width
\[
W_{n,m,\tau}=O_{\mathbb P_{P,n}}\!\left(\ell\min\{1,[m\log(40m)/n]^\varkappa\}+D\tau^{\beta/4}\right)
\]
after the empty-region totalization is corrected.  What is not established is a matching lower bound over all honest systems or the necessary-and-sufficient shrinking criterion.
